questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

Having been found (a)/ guilty of fraud and (b)/ theft Harshal was (c)/sentenced to three year’s imprisonment. (d)/ No error
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option C: D.

  • The error is in part (d), where "three year’s imprisonment" is used.
  • The correct form should be "three years' imprisonment" because "years" is plural, so the possessive form should be "years'".
  • Here are example sentences using numeral + possessive case + noun:
    • Two days' notice is required before the meeting.
    • Five years' experience is needed for this position.
    • Three weeks' vacation is allotted to each employee.

Corrected Sentence: "Having been found guilty of fraud and theft, Harshal was sentenced to three years' imprisonment."

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

We can trust (a)/ the Media247 channel (b)/ for the last news (c)/ of this hour. (d)/ No error
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option C: C.

  • The error is in part (c), where "the last news" is used.
  • The correct phrase should be "the latest news" because "latest" refers to the most recent news, while "last" refers to the final item in a series.
    • Examples:
      • The last movie I watched was amazing.
      • Have you heard the latest news about the company?

Corrected Sentence: "We can trust the Media247 channel for the latest news of this hour."

Direction: In the following question, a sentence has been divided into four parts, one of which may contain an error. Identify that part and mark it as your answer. If the given sentence is correct as it is, mark ‘No Error’ as the answer. Ignore errors in punctuation, if any.

Kamalpreet went to (A)/ the nearing supermarket (B)/ to buy groceries as her parents were (C)/ expecting guests in the evening. (D)/No error
questions.explanation:
The error is in part (B), where "nearing" is used.

  • The correct word should be "nearby" because "nearby" is the correct adjective to describe "not far away in distance", while "nearing" is a verb indicating something coming closer in time or distance.
    • Examples:
      • The storm is nearing, and we should prepare for it.
      • There is a grocery store nearby.

Hence, option C is the correct choice.

Corrected Sentence: "Kamalpreet went to the nearby supermarket to buy groceries as her parents were expecting guests in the evening."

Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (e), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

The faster Jamal (a)/ completes the project (b)/ assigned to him, the largest (c)/ will be his share in this company. (d)/ No error
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option C: C.

  • The error is in part (c), where "largest" is used.
  • The correct word should be "larger" because in comparisons involving the phrase "the faster... the larger", the comparative form of the adjective "large" (i.e., "larger") should be used.
  • Here are examples of relative increase and decrease:
    • The more you exercise, the stronger you become.
    • The higher the demand, the higher the price.
    • The less you sleep, the more tired you feel.

Corrected Sentence: "The faster Jamal completes the project, the larger will be his share in this company."

questions.question:

questions.question:
Direction : In the following question, a sentence is given, divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part may contain an error. Mark the part having an error as your answer. If none of the parts contain an error, mark “No error” as your answer.

The more important day of a person's life is not necessarily(A)/ the day he was born or the day he graduated,(B)/ but rather the day when he realised his true purpose and began(C)/ to live his life with passion, intention, and a deep sense of fulfilment.(D) No error (E)
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: Option D (A)

  • The error lies in part (A): "The more important day of a person's life is not necessarily."
  • The comparison made in the sentence is between "the day" and all other days in a person's life, which requires the superlative degree "most" instead of "more."
  • "Most" is used when comparing one thing to all others, and "more" is used for comparisons between two things.

Corrected Sentence: The most important day of a person's life is not necessarily the day he was born or the day he graduated, but rather the day when he realised his true purpose and began to live his life with passion, intention, and a deep sense of fulfilment.

questions.question:

The music at the concert was so loudly that it(A)/ reverberated through my entire body,(B)/ drowning out all other sounds and making(C)/ it impossible to hear anything else.(D) No error(E)
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: Option D (A)

  • The error lies in part (A): "The music at the concert was so loudly that it."
  • The adverb "loudly" is incorrect here because we need an adjective to modify "music," not an adverb. The correct word is "loud."
  • "So loud" is the proper structure to show the extent of the music's volume.

Corrected Sentence: The music at the concert was so loud that it reverberated through my entire body, drowning out all other sounds and making it impossible to hear anything else

questions.question:
Directions: Study the following sentences and mark the erroneous part as your answer. In case there is no error, mark option (E), that is, ‘No Error’ as your answer.

Since there is a little(a)/ milk left in the jar, (b) /you cannot make three (c)/ cups of tea with it. (d)/ No error
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: Option A (a)

  • The error lies in part (a): "Since there is a little."
  • The sentence states, "...you cannot make three cups of tea with it," which implies that there is almost no milk, or an insufficient amount of milk. 
    "A little" means a small amount but some (positive connotation, implying there is enough to use).
    "Little" means hardly any (negative connotation, implying there is not enough). 
    Since the context implies the amount is insufficient, "a little" should be replaced with "little". 

Corrected Sentence: Since there is little milk left in the jar, you cannot make three cups of tea with it.

questions.question:
Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.

No country has so much diversity as India, encompassing languages, cultures, religions, and landscapes.
questions.explanation:
The given statement is grammatically incorrect and the error lies in the option “No country has so much” and the error is related to the “Adjective”.

  • The sentence is comparing the diversity of India to that of other countries.
  • When making this kind of comparison, it's customary to use the phrase "no other + country" to emphasize that India has the most diversity among all countries.

○ Examples:

■ Correct: No other city has as many parks as New York.

■ Incorrect: No city has as many parks as New York.

Hence, use “No other country " in place of "No country ".

The correct statement after the correction will be: No other country has so much diversity as India, encompassing languages, cultures, religions, and landscapes.

questions.question:
Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.

Suddenly he plumped himself right into the arms of a tallest, ungainly man, who had crossed from the other side.
options: right into the arms of a tallest
questions.explanation:
The given sentence is grammatically incorrect, and the error lies in the option “right into the arms of a tallest, ungainly man.” The error is related to the use of the superlative adjective.

  • In the given question, "a tallest" should be corrected to "the tallest."
  • When using a superlative adjective like "tallest," we use the definite article "the" instead of the indefinite article "a."
    • Example: She spoke to the tallest person in the room.

Hence, "a tallest" must be replaced by "the tallest" to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Correct sentence: Suddenly he plumped himself right into the arms of the tallest, ungainly man, who had crossed from the other side

questions.question:
Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.


Our warden strictly told us not to arrive latter than 8 o'clock.
questions.explanation:
The given statement is grammatically incorrect and the error lies in the option “to arrive latter

” and the error is related to the “Adjective”.

 

  • Later:

○ "Later" is an adverb that refers to a point in time that comes after the present, a specified time, or another event. It is used to indicate time or sequence.

■ Example: "I will meet you later in the evening."

  • Latter:

○ "Latter" is an adjective that is used to refer to the second of two things or the last mentioned in a list of two. It is used when you are comparing or contrasting two items.

■ Example: "I have two options: a red shirt and a blue one. I prefer the latter."

  • The word we need here is "later," which means a point in time that is subsequent to the current time.

Hence, use “later" in place of "latter".

 

The correct statement after the correction will be: Our warden strictly told us not to arrive later than 8 o'clock.

questions.question:
Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.

She discovered a letter, tucked away in a dusty attic, elder to any living memory in town.
questions.explanation:
The given statement is grammatically incorrect and the error lies in the option “a dusty attic, elder to” and the error is related to the “Adjective”.

 

  • “Elder" is a comparative term used to compare the age of two people or things.

○ For example, you might say, "He is elder to his brother," to indicate that he is the older of the two siblings.

  • "Older" is used to indicate a comparative age without specifying a direct comparison to another person or thing. It is the appropriate word to use when comparing something to "any living memory in town," as there isn't a specific comparison being made.
  • In this sentence, you want to express that the letter is older than any living memory in town, so "older" is the correct word to use.

 

Hence, use “older than" in place of "elder to".

 

The correct statement after the correction will be: She discovered a letter, tucked away in a dusty attic, older than any living memory in town.

questions.question:
Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.

In a perfect world, achieving the most ideal balance between work, life, and personal fulfilment remains challenging.
options: In a perfect world, achieving the most
questions.explanation:
The given statement is grammatically incorrect and the error lies in the option “In a perfect world, achieving the most” and the error is related to the “Adjective”.

 

  • Some adjectives already convey the highest or lowest degree of a particular quality, and adding a superlative form can be redundant or illogical.

○ Here are some examples of such adjectives:

■ Perfect: "Perfect" means the highest level of excellence, so saying something is "the most perfect" would be redundant. Instead, you would simply say "perfect."

■ Infinite: "Infinite" means limitless, so there is no "more infinite" or "most infinite."

■ Dead: "Dead" means not alive, so there is no "deader" or "deadest."

  • The word "Ideal" already implies that something is perfect and cannot be compared or ranked in terms of degree.

○ It's incorrect to use "most" with "ideal" because idealness doesn't have degrees like "more" or "most."

 

Hence, omit “most”.

 

The correct statement after the correction will be: In a perfect world, achieving the ideal balance between work, life, and personal fulfilment remains challenging.

Direction : In the following question, a sentence is given, divided into four parts. Out of the four parts, one part may contain an error. Mark the part having an error as your answer. If none of the parts contain an error, mark “No error” as your answer.

questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: B

  • The phrase "a certain prescription drugs" is incorrect.
  • The phrase "a certain" is used with singular nouns (e.g., a certain drug), whereas "certain" (without "a") is used with plural nouns (e.g., certain drugs).
  • Since "drugs" is plural, the correct phrase here is "certain prescription drugs" instead of "a certain prescription drugs."

Corrected Sentence: A spiked drink might seem harmless, but if a person was taking certain prescription drugs, it could be dangerous.

questions.explanation:

Diamond is a remarkable material, possessing a unique combination of properties(A)/ that make it highly desirable for a wide range of applications,(B)/ including its exceptional hardness, which is evidenced by its ability to scratch(C)/ and cut through virtually any material, making it harder than any other metal known to man.(D) No error (E)
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: Option C (D)

  • The error lies in part (D): "making it harder than any other metal known to man."
  • Since diamond is not a metal, it should be compared to "any metal" rather than "any other metal." The correct structure excludes the comparison within the class of metals and refers to it being harder than any metal.
    • Example:
      • Gold is costlier than 'any other' metal. Here, 'any other' separates gold from the whole class of metals. Diamond is harder than any metal. Here, 'any metal' is used since 'Diamond' is not a metal. Hence, the correct option is C.

Corrected Sentence: Diamond is a remarkable material, possessing a unique combination of properties that make it highly desirable for a wide range of applications, including its exceptional hardness, which is evidenced by its ability to scratch and cut through virtually any material, making it harder than any metal known to man.

After having spent countless hours studying and practising, I had finally achieved a level of proficiency in playing the piano that(A)/ I had always dreamed of, but little did I know that there was still so much more perfect(B)/ to be done in terms of mastering the nuances of tone, dynamics,(C)/ and expression that only comes with years of dedicated practice and experience.(D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation:
In Part B of the sentence, remove the word 'more' before 'perfect,' as some words cannot be used in the comparative or superlative form. The sentence should read, "I had always dreamed of, but little did I know that there was still so much perfect."

  • Here is a list of words that cannot be used in the comparative or superlative degree: Supreme, impossible, absolute, ideal, everlasting, eternal, rectangular, square, round, major, minor, complete, entire, chief, extreme, excellent, ulterior, universal, unique, last, and final.

Corrected Sentence: After having spent countless hours studying and practising, I had finally achieved a level of proficiency in playing the piano that I had always dreamed of, but little did I know that there was still so much perfect to be done in terms of mastering the nuances of tone, dynamics, and expression that only comes with years of dedicated practice and experience.

Hence, the correct answer is Option C (B).

These kind of projects, which involve complex research

  • "These" is a demonstrative adjective that is used to indicate or point to specific objects or people in a sentence.

○ It helps provide context or clarify which items you are referring to. D

○ Demonstrative adjectives answer the question "Which one?" or "Which ones?" and can be used to show proximity or distance in relation to the speaker.

questions.question:
Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error mark option (E) as your answer.

The government of India has allowed field trials of two new varieties of indigenous develop GM brinjals in eight states of the country.
questions.explanation:
The given statement is grammatically incorrect and the error lies in the option “of indigenous develop”. 

  • The verb "develop" is a transitive or intransitive verb, which means it can have an object or not.
  • When we want to use a verb as an adjective to modify a noun, we need to use the past participle of the verb, which is formed by adding -ed to the base form of the verb "develop".
  • The noun "GM brinjals" is a plural noun, which means it refers to more than one genetically modified brinjal. 
  • We need to use an adverb to modify the past participle "developed".

Hence, use "of indigenously developed" in place of "of indigenous develop" to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Correct sentence: The government of India has allowed field trials of two new varieties of indigenously developed GM brinjals in eight states of the country.

The error lies in the use of "harder" instead of "hardest."

In the corrected sentence, "hardest" accurately conveys the highest level of difficulty, which aligns with the intended meaning.

questions.question:
Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error mark option (E) as your answer.

In the northern suburbs of Bengaluru, home to the bulk of the information technology industry, the water crisis is even worst.
questions.explanation:
The given sentence is grammatically incorrect and the error lies in the option “is even worst”. The error is related to the “Adjectives”.

In the given question, the error is in "is even worst" because of the incorrect use of the degree of the adjective 'worst'.

  • "Worst" is the superlative form of the adjective and is used when comparing three or more things. In the given sentence, 'worse' is used because it is used to compare two things (the water crisis in the northern suburbs of Bengaluru) and implies a comparative degree.
  • In the given sentence, we are comparing the water crisis in the northern suburbs to other areas or situations. So, we will use 'worse' here in place of 'worst'.
  • Example: My brother is bad at basketball, but honestly I'm worse.

Hence, "is even worst" must be replaced by "is even worse" to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Correct sentence: In the northern suburbs of Bengaluru, home to the bulk of the information technology industry, the water crisis is even worse.
